props.note: the source does not say which of these catalysts, other than the one used, were tested, how they were made or how active they were

props.name: zinc oxide from decomposition of zinc carbonate in air at 300 °C
at this temperature hydrogen and carbon monoxide are adsorbed as ions (cited)
props.note: cited from Gubokawa and Toyama (hydrogen) and Keier and Chizhikova (carbon monoxide)
props.statement: At this temperature both hydrogen and carbon monoxide are adsorbed on zinc oxide as ions, so energetic electrons may be expected to influence adsorption and reaction rates.

props.name: CO2 formation also increased under irradiation, but less than methanol
props.statement: The amount of carbon dioxide formed also increased under irradiation, but to a lesser extent than the yield of methanol; the maximum G for carbon dioxide was 0.56 at 201 °C.

props.name: the industrial process uses high pressures, 200 atm; not needed at low temperature
props.statement: Since reaction was sought at low temperatures where the equilibrium favours methanol, the high pressures of the industrial process, 200 atm, were not necessary.

props.name: irradiation does not greatly influence the normal reaction mechanism
props.statement: Since the lower temperature limit for the radiation effect is very close to that for normal thermal catalysis, irradiation of the catalyst does not greatly influence the normal reaction mechanism.

props.name: no effect of radiation above 250 °C or below 175 °C
props.note: the runs outside 175-250 °C are not reported individually
props.statement: No effect of radiation was observed at temperatures above 250 °C or below 175 °C.

props.name: of pure ZnO and ZnO-chromium oxide catalysts only one was active below 250 °C
props.statement: Of the catalysts investigated (pure zinc oxide and zinc oxide admixed with chromium oxide) only one was active at temperatures below 250 °C; it was used for the radiation study.

props.name: the effect of radiation on the methanol rate is quite small and masked at higher temperatures
props.statement: The effect of radiation on the rate of methanol formation over zinc oxide is quite small and is masked at higher temperatures.

props.name: selectivity for methanol improved below 260 °C; methane and CO2 also formed
props.statement: Besides methanol, methane and carbon dioxide were formed; the selectivity of the catalyst for methanol synthesis was improved by working at temperatures below 260 °C.

props.name: catalytic activity of semiconducting oxides is linked to their ability to act as electron sources or sinks; radiation expected to affect it
props.note: presented as well known; the premise of the study
props.statement: Semiconducting oxides such as zinc oxide, nickel oxide and vanadium pentoxide are an important class of heterogeneous catalysts whose activity is closely linked with their ability to act as electron sources or sinks; since radiation modifies the electrical properties of semiconductors, it is anticipated to affect their catalytic activity.

props.name: standard free energy of CO + H2 to methanol negative only below 150 °C; reaction rapid only above 350 °C
props.note: stated without a calculation or reference in this letter
props.statement: At temperatures where the reaction proceeds at a reasonable rate the equilibrium favours carbon monoxide and hydrogen: the standard free energy of the reaction becomes negative only below 150 °C, whereas the reaction is rapid only above 350 °C; activating the catalyst at lower temperatures by radiation would greatly facilitate the reaction.

props.name: 3:1 mixture of hydrogen and carbon monoxide

h2_co_ratio.as_reported: A 3 : 1 mixture of hydrogen and carbon
h2_co_ratio.note: 3 : 1 hydrogen to carbon monoxide; basis not stated

props.name: the radiation-induced increase in methanol rate is due to direct participation of freshly produced electrons
props.statement: The observed increase in the rate of methanol formation over irradiated zinc oxide may be ascribed to direct participation of electrons freshly produced by radiation.

props.name: participation of holes seems unlikely
props.statement: Participation of holes in the radiation effect seems unlikely, since holes are not present in unirradiated zinc oxide, an n-type semiconductor.

props.name: about 20% of radiation-induced electrons are effective and about 20 eV frees one electron
props.statement: About 20 per cent of the electrons induced by irradiation are effective in promoting catalytic reaction and about 20 eV are required to free one electron; with these assumptions the G value is consistent with electron participation.
